name: literature-review-tools
cost: Skill free. Some tools need API keys
works_with: Claude Code, plus other agents that can load a SKILL.md
short: Finds papers, fetches legal open-access PDFs and installs research tools like PaperQA2 or MinerU for you.
what: A literature review skill with three modes. Look up searches six scholarly indexes (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, PubMed, Europe PMC, arXiv) and fetches open-access full text with no install and no API key. Recommend picks a tool from a catalog of 70+ open-source projects. Run installs a tool such as MinerU, PaperQA2 or ASReview in its own Python environment and runs it.
who: Researchers, students and anyone writing a literature review or related-work section with a coding agent. Its install steps are written for Claude Code.
needs: Python 3. The search scripts and the launcher use only the standard library
Optional: uv, which the launcher uses when it's there
API keys only for some tools. GPT Researcher's web UI needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `TAVILY_API_KEY`, and the PaperQA2 steps need `OPENAI_API_KEY`

steps.title: Install as a Claude Code plugin
steps.text: This pulls in the skill and the launcher scripts in one step.

steps.title: Or copy the skill folder
steps.text: For one project only, copy it into `.claude/skills/` inside that project instead.

steps.title: Restart your agent
steps.text: The skill loads on its own when your request is about literature review work. For other agents, point your skills loader at `skills/literature-review-tools/SKILL.md`.

try.label: From the README
try.text:
find recent papers on <your topic>

Or:
get me the PDF for this DOI
does this citation exist?
what should I use to turn PDFs into Markdown for an LLM?

watch: Run mode installs tools into separate environments under `~/.lit-review-tools/` and keeps API keys in `~/.lit-review-tools/.env`. Your agent runs these installs through its shell.
Some tools are big. marker and docling pull in PyTorch.
GPT Researcher and STORM start long-running local web servers (ports 8000 and 8501).
The README says nothing in it gets round a paywall. Closed papers are reported as closed.
